questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about shadows?
choices: Shadows change shape when the light source is moved
Shadows are formed only by opaque objects
Shadows are formed by all types of objects
questions.solution: Shadows are formed when an opaque object blocks light. Transparent and translucent objects do not form shadows or form very faint ones. Shadows can change shape when the light source is moved, but they are not always dark. Therefore, the correct statement is that shadows are formed only by opaque objects.

hi.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा छाया के बारे में सही कथन है?
choices: जब प्रकाश स्रोत गति करता है तो छाया का आकार बदल जाता है
छायाएँ केवल अपारदर्शी वस्तुओं द्वारा बनती हैं
सभी प्रकार की वस्तुओं द्वारा छायाएँ बनती हैं
hi.solution: छायाएँ तब बनती हैं जब अपारदर्शी वस्तु प्रकाश को रोक देती है। पारदर्शी और अर्धपारदर्शी वस्तुएँ छायाएँ नहीं बनाती हैं या बहुत हल्की छायाएँ बनाती हैं। जब प्रकाश स्रोत गति करता है तो छाया का आकार बदल सकता है, लेकिन वे हमेशा गहरी नहीं होती। इसलिए सही कथन यह है कि छायाएँ केवल अपारदर्शी वस्तुओं द्वारा बनती हैं।
hi.critique: Translation is accurate and maintains the original meaning, technical terms are appropriately used in Hindi.

questions.stem: A student wants to see a shadow of a book on a wall. Which of the following is NOT necessary for forming a shadow?
questions.solution: A shadow is formed when an opaque object blocks light from reaching a screen. A transparent object allows light to pass through and does not form a shadow. A source of light and a screen are necessary for the formation of a shadow. Therefore, a transparent object is not necessary for forming a shadow.

questions.stem: What is the main reason for the formation of a shadow?
choices: Light is absorbed by the object
Light is reflected by the object
Light is scattered by the object

questions.solution: A shadow is formed when an object blocks light from reaching a surface. Light is not absorbed, reflected, or scattered in a way that prevents the formation of a shadow. The main reason is that the object blocks the light. Therefore, the correct answer is that light is blocked by the object.

questions.stem: In Activity 11.6, a student uses a comb with a slit to create a thin beam of light. What happens when this beam is reflected by a mirror?
choices: The beam continues in a straight line without change
The beam gets absorbed by the mirror
The beam splits into multiple beams
questions.solution: When a light beam is reflected by a mirror, it changes direction according to the law of reflection. The beam does not continue in a straight line, nor does it get absorbed or split into multiple beams. The change in direction of the light beam is a clear indication of reflection. Therefore, the beam changes direction when it reflects off the mirror.

questions.stem: A student placed a transparent object in front of a light source and observed a faint shadow. What could be the reason for this observation?
questions.solution: Translucent objects allow some light to pass through but scatter it, resulting in a faint shadow. Transparent objects do not form shadows because light passes through them completely. Opaque objects form dark shadows, and mirrors reflect light, not form shadows. Therefore, the object being translucent explains the faint shadow observed.
